Bharatiya Janata Party Spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia addresses a press conference, in New Delhi, on November 16, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday (November 16, 2026), referring to the ‘Bharat Summit’ organised by the Congress in Telangana’s Hyderabad on November 14, accused the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party of bringing together “foreign anti-India forces” to undermine India’s sovereignty and democratic institutions,
“These platforms are used to spread hatred against Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji , to create anarchy and foment instability in India,” alleged BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia at a press conference, questioning the decision to give a platform to Giacomo Filibeck, an Italian politician currently serving as secretary general of the Party of European Socialists.
“From this platform, he says, ‘vote chor , gaddi chhod (vote thieves, vacate the seat)’. An anarchic and immature Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, makes similar statements in India. But look at the irony. From an Indian platform, a foreigner challenges the Indian mandate and mocks it. And what is even more unfortunate? Rahul Gandhi does not stop Giacomo Filibeck,” Mr. Bhatia said, alleging that the Congress leader “clapped” and “laughed” in response.
“India’s interests took a back seat” in Congress-ruled Telangana, Mr. Bhatia said, adding that investment summits organised in BJP-ruled States attracted foreign investors and ideologues to discuss investment opportunities.
“The Congress party loses 99 elections, but does not introspect. Rahul Gandhi should reduce his foreign visits a little. If he visits India’s villages and cities and interacts with Indians instead, he will understand why 140 crore Indians bless the Bharatiya Janata Party,” Mr. Bhatia said.
The Telangana government’s website stated the event was organised using government funds, he said. “All of us would like to know how much government money you have spent to criticise India. Since you take credit for this event, also tell us how much the Congress party spent on it,” he said.
The BJP leader questioned Mr. Filibeck’s credentials. “This is a person with a highly controversial history...Will Rahul Gandhi take the trouble to tell the country that you have become so weak that you cannot win elections on your own? You need the assistance of foreign forces. Do you support the kind of statement made by Mr. Filibeck from an Indian platform, or do you not?” he said.
Mr. Bhatia accused Mr. Gandhi of suffering from “a disease called hatred for Modi ji ”, and alleged that Mr. Gandhi’s hatred had blinded him. The Modi government was strong and transparent, and worked in the national interest, he said.
